memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the woven garments worn for ministering in the sanctuary, both the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when serving as priests. The Israelites had done all the work just as the Lord had commanded Moses. Moses inspected the work and saw that they had done it just as the Lord had commanded. So Moses blessed them." - Exod 39:41-43 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses inspected everything, found it done exactly as God had commanded, and blessed them.

The inspection was thorough. He looked at all of it. And what he found was faithfulness.

This chapter ends the way it began — with obedience. That phrase, "just as the Lord commanded," has run through the whole passage like a heartbeat.

Notice what Moses did not say: "good enough," or "impressive effort." He blessed them. There was joy in the assessment, not merely approval.

It is a foretaste of something greater. Jesus told of a master who said to his servant, "Well done, good and faithful servant" (Matt 25:21). And we are told that each of us will give an account before the judgement seat of Christ (2 Cor 5:10) — not a trial for our salvation, which is settled in Him, but a reckoning of how we served.

Live today knowing that inspection is coming and blessing is possible. Not because we can build perfectly, but because Christ has made us acceptable and the Spirit works in us to will and to act (Phil 2:13).

The tabernacle stood ready. In the next chapter, glory would fill it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. If your work were inspected today, what would it show?
2. Are you serving for human approval or God's "well done"?
3. What one thing would you want to change before the inspection comes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let my life be found faithful. Work in me what pleases You, and let me hear Your well done. Amen.
